title: Robust A/B Experiment Summary
prompt:
Analyze experiment rows represented as mappings with `variant`, `exposed`, `metric`, and optional `country`. Metrics are finite numbers or `None`. Retain only exposed rows whose variant is A or B and whose metric is not missing. A missing country never excludes a row from the overall summary.

`ab_summary(rows)` returns a mapping with `lift` and `p_value`. Define lift as `(mean_B - mean_A) / mean_A`; it is NaN if either group is absent or mean_A is zero. A singleton group can still have a defined lift. For p_value, require at least two observations in each group and use the standard error `sqrt(sample_var_A / n_A + sample_var_B / n_B)`, where sample variance uses denominator `n-1`. Return the two-sided normal-tail approximation `erfc(abs(mean_B - mean_A) / (sqrt(2) * standard_error))`. If the standard error is zero, return 1.0 for equal means and 0.0 otherwise. If either group has fewer than two rows, p_value is NaN independently of whether lift is defined. A zero baseline mean invalidates relative lift, not the absolute-mean test.

`SegmentLiftReport(rows)` pre-aggregates valid rows with a non-missing country and exposes `lift(country)` with the same relative-lift rule. Unknown, one-sided, or zero-baseline segments return NaN.

This is a local numerical reporting helper. Its p-value is a normal approximation using unequal-variance standard errors, not an exact finite-sample Welch t-test; experimental design, repeated testing, and metric selection remain separate questions.

example.input: two exposed A and two exposed B records
example.output: a mapping containing lift and p_value
example.reasoning: The summary separates exposure filtering from metric validity.

background_note: General preparation exercise. A bounded Notion/source audit did not recover an original interview prompt for this exact local contract. The former unverified OpenAI tag has been removed; technical documentation supports the method, not an interview occurrence. SciPy documents unequal-variance Welch testing; this exercise deliberately uses a normal tail rather than the finite-degrees-of-freedom t distribution. Relative lift and significance are independent outputs with separate undefined cases.
